title: West Bengal's Budget Shift: What Cuts to Minority Welfare Funds Mean
description: The new West Bengal government has significantly reduced funds for the Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education (MAME) Department. The budget for the departmen.

faq.q: What is the Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education (MAME) Department?
faq.a: It is a state government department in West Bengal responsible for the welfare, development, and education of minority communities, including administering various schemes and grants.

faq.q: How much was the budget cut for the MAME Department?
faq.a: The allocation for the MAME Department for FY 2026-27 has been cut by 62%, from ₹5,713.61 crore in the interim budget to ₹2,175.43 crore in the current budget.

faq.q: Which specific schemes are most affected?
faq.a: The Aikyashree Scholarship (50% cut), housing for destitute minority women (zero allocation), Sabooj Sathi (reduced from ₹100 crore to ₹15.5 crore), and general development and welfare schemes for minorities (reduced to ₹21 crore) are significantly impacted.

faq.q: What is the government's stated reason for these changes?
faq.a: The Chief Minister has reportedly emphasized encouraging minority children to pursue mainstream education and professions like doctors or engineers.
